does: Forms a soft mixture into even pieces that hold together when they are cooked.

intro.what: This shaping method forms chilled soft mixtures into smooth even portions.
intro.why: It teaches you to judge cohesion and use minimal handling for a lighter texture.

how: Chill the mixture first. A cold mixture holds its shape and does not stick.
For quenelles, dip a pair of spoons in hot water, scoop the mixture with the first, and pass it back and forth between them until its sides are smooth.
For patties and balls, wet your hands and press lightly, only until the piece holds.
Make every piece the same size, so that they cook in the same time.

cues.text: Pieces of one size with smooth surfaces and no cracks.
The piece holds when it is lifted, and gives a little under a finger.

mistakes.mistake: Working the mixture for too long or pressing it hard, which makes it dense and tough.
mistakes.fix: Handle it as little as you can.

mistakes.mistake: Shaping a warm, loose mixture, which sticks to everything and falls apart in the pot.
mistakes.fix: Chill it until it is firm before you start.

quiz.question: Why make shaped portions similar in size?
choices: To keep their cooking rates similar.
To make all mixtures equally firm.
To replace chilling a loose mixture.
quiz.because: Size consistency limits differences in how each portion responds to heat.

quiz.question: How are spoon-shaped quenelles smoothed?
choices: Shape only with the edge of a single dry spoon.
Pass the mixture between spoons dipped in hot water.
Press the mixture onto the board with a dry spoon.
quiz.because: Warm wet spoons release the mixture as it is passed between them to form smooth sides.

quiz.question: Which feel suggests a portion is well shaped?
choices: It runs off the spoon without a shape.
It is tightly packed and rigid.
It holds when lifted and gives a little when pressed.
quiz.because: A little give with sufficient cohesion avoids both slumping and excessive compaction.

quiz.question: A warm loose mixture sticks and falls apart. What should happen first?
choices: Chill it until firm before shaping.
Press it harder while it stays warm.
Make larger portions from the same loose mixture.
quiz.because: Chilling gives the mixture more body so it can hold its shape with gentler handling.
